entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Volcatius Tullus was a Roman politician who served as consul in 33 BC and later became an enemy of Julius Caesar. In 50 BCE, he played a crucial role in the conspiracy against Caesar's life.

Tullus was born into a noble family and rose to prominence through his military service and political connections. He was elected consul in 33 BC, but his term was short-lived due to his opposition to Caesar's growing power.

The legacy of Lucius Volcatius Tullus can be seen in the tumultuous years following Caesar's assassination, which led to a power struggle between the Roman Senate and the First Triumvirate. His actions ultimately contributed to the downfall of the Roman Republic and paved the way for the rise of the Roman Empire.

Like this: 'The conspirators' plan was not just about killing Caesar, but also about reshaping the future of Rome.'
